subject: railgunCarrier
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: six-wheeled railgun carrier braced on stabiliser legs.
Style: low-poly sci-fi military.

spec.name: Longspear Railgun Carrier
spec.description: A six-wheeled low-poly sci-fi military railgun carrier with a long twin-rail cannon, braced on four hydraulic stabiliser legs.
spec.layout: A long angular 6x6 carrier facing +Z. Front: a wedge-nosed armoured cab (z 2.6 to 4.4) with a slanted glass visor glowing cyan, headlights and a roof sensor mast. Behind the cab, a low flat chassis deck (top y 1.5) carrying a rotating turret ring at z -1.2 on which sits a boxy gun cradle with the long twin-rail railgun pointing forward over the cab, barrel tip near z 5.0, raised about 12 degrees, with a rear capacitor bank with glowing cyan coils behind it. Six big chunky wheels (three per side, axles at z 3.2, 0.4, -2.6, x +-1.45, radius 0.62, hubs on y 0.62) sit under fenders; the wheels touch the floor. Four stabiliser legs fold out diagonally from the chassis at the corners (x +-2.0 to 2.6) with pads on the floor (y 0). Style: faceted low-poly sci-fi military, olive-drab and dark gunmetal panels, yellow hazard stripes on legs and fenders, cyan glow on rails, coils and visor, small separate parts for bolts, vents, lights, decals and number stencils.

parts.builds: Main hull and frame: a long faceted lower hull box with sloped front and rear plates, flat deck top at y 1.5 with panel seams, vent grilles, bolts, hullDark skirt plates, rear tow hooks and rear lamps, hazard-striped bumper, side tool boxes, a short ring plinth at turretRing, fuel/ammo hatches and white stencil number decals. Colours hull, hullDark, hullLight, darkSteel, hazard, red, decalWhite.
parts.attaches: Cab starts at its front face (z 3.0); turret sits on turretRing; wheels and legs hang off the sides at the axle and leg mounts.

parts.builds: Armoured wedge cab: faceted sloped nose, angled cyan-glow visor (glassDark with neonCyan frame lines), side armour plates with hazard chevrons, twin headlights (lightWhite, glowing), roof sensor mast with dish and antenna, smoke launchers, mirrors, door seams and handles, lower bumper with tow loops. Colours hull, hullLight, gunmetal, glassDark, neonCyan, lightWhite, hazard, steel.
parts.attaches: Sits on chassis front at z 3.0 and chassisTop; roof at cabRoof; the railgun passes over the cab roof above it.

parts.builds: Six chunky low-poly wheels (octagonal tyres in tire with tread block parts, rim and hub discs in rim, bolt rings, hubcaps with a small hazard dot), axles and suspension arms in darkSteel, and fender arches over each wheel in hullDark with hazard stripe edges and mud flaps in rubber. Wheels touch y 0. Wheel groups ride wheelFL.. wheelRR joints.
parts.attaches: Axles at axleFront, axleMid, axleRear on the chassis flanks at x +-1.45; fenders attach to the chassis sides.

parts.builds: Four deployed stabiliser legs: each has a chassis-side bracket and hinge block, an upper hydraulic arm angled outward and down, a telescoping steel piston rod with a ring collar, a diagonal brace strut, and a wide octagonal foot pad on y 0 with rubber underplate and bolts. Hazard-black stripes on arms, cyan status light on each hinge. Joints legFL, legFR, legRL, legRR. Pads at about x +-2.6, z 2.4 and -3.6.
parts.attaches: Brackets bolt to chassis flanks at legFrontL / legRearL mounts (mirrored in x); feet on the floor outside the wheels.

parts.builds: Rotating turret and railgun: low octagonal turret base ring on turretRing, boxy gun cradle with side plates and trunnion pivots at gunPivot, a long twin-rail barrel (two parallel gunmetal rails with a glowing neonCyan inner channel and strip, stepped rail clamps every half metre, muzzle brake block at muzzle), raised about 12 degrees so the tip reaches z 5.0 y 3.0, rear capacitor bank box with copper coils and glowing cyan ring rings, cooling fins, hydraulic elevation cylinders, ammo slug rack, ladder and handrails on the turret roof, hazard muzzle band, small warning decals. Colours gunmetal, darkSteel, steel, neonCyan, copper, hazard, hull.
parts.attaches: Turret base on turretRing (chassis deck y 1.5); gun pivot at gunPivot; barrel passes over cabRoof, staying above y 2.8 at the cab.

calls.reasoning:
I need to figure out the context type for buildStabilisers since it's module-provided rather than imported, so I'll define a local interface instead to avoid naming conflicts. I'm sketching the leg layout, iterating per side and front/rear position.

I'm working out hinge positions, pad placement, and clearance checks against the wheels so the legs don't intersect them, then planning the rod and cylinder geometry for the pads and feet with layered rubber/steel sections.

Now I'm defining the arm and piston segments between hinge, elbow, knee, and pad points, adding brace struts and bracket connections, and setting up hazard stripe markers as short cylindrical bands along the arm.

I'm also placing the pad with bolts around its top ring, adding a glowing light at the hinge, and building the bracket plate and hinge block geometry with their own bolts.

Working out the hinge arm start point and mirroring the piston direction for front versus rear pads, then deciding most tilted parts are easier to represent as rods than oriented boxes before writing it all out.

I'm figuring out how to handle the Ctx type reference in buildRailgun without an explicit import, deciding whether to treat it as implicitly provided by the module scope or declare a local fallback type to avoid conflicts.

Now I'm working through the geometry of the turret and gun joints, computing the barrel's pitch angle and direction vectors so the barrel tip lands at the correct height without exceeding the bounding box, adjusting the pivot offset and length to balance clearance against the target tip position.

I'll settle on barrel centre offset -0.45 with length extending to z 5.4, close enough despite being slightly over the box. Now I'm working out how to orient the barrel part using a direction/axis helper so the geometry aligns along z with up vector control, then setting up a helper function to build position vectors.

Still laying out turret geometry...

Actually simpler to build the capacitor bank as a cylinder along z with coil rings wrapped around it, using a small helper to orient cylinder geometry along the z-axis. For the barrel, I'm adding two rails at x ±0.16 as rectangular beams running along the gun's length.

Still placing barrel details... adding the inner cyan glow channel between rails, thin cyan strips on rail tops, periodic steel clamps every 0.5 units straddling both rails, and a muzzle brake block at the barrel tip with a hazard-striped ring band near it.

Now I'm adding the breech block connecting the gun cradle to the rails, then setting up a pair of hydraulic elevation cylinders linking the turret body to the gun mount using bone-anchored rod geometry. Finally I'm planning a roof ladder and handrail posts along the rear sides of the turret.

Then I'm detailing more interior features: a vertical rear ladder with rungs, a side ammo rack holding steel slug cylinders, cooling fins along the top of the cap bank, small hazard decal plates, rear vents, and an octagonal roof hatch cylinder.

Checking the cap bank's position relative to the turret body, I confirm it mostly sits outside the rear boundary in world coordinates, so placement should be fine. I'm planning to import a glow helper to wrap the cyan-lit parts, use the established palette, and keep the total part count near 150, while setting up a vector helper to compute perpendicular directions for angled placements.

I'm defining helper functions for placing gun parts (boxes and cylinders) relative to the gun's pivot and direction vectors, plus separate helpers for turret-mounted boxes and cylinders in world space, along with a glow wrapper for emissive parts. Now I'm laying out the copper coil rings and interleaved cyan rings along the barrel using torus geometry at staggered depths.

I'm adding dark steel end caps on the barrel, figuring out rail clamp spacing along the rail length, and sketching sloped turret side plates as angled boxes before writing it all out.
